caption: In an outdoor backyard, a staircase built from stacked brown cardboard boxes descends toward the right, set against an unchanged green hedge, leafy tree branches, and an overturned yellow pot resting on grass. At the upper left, a person's fingers grip the top end of a chain of shiny metal spheres, holding it steady while the chain pays out downward. The spheres tumble over the edge of the highest step and cascade in sequence along the structure. Leading spheres travel down the vertical faces and rebound off the step edges. They then drop into the air between steps as they descend. Following spheres emerge one after another from the hand, stretching the chain longer as it feeds over each tier. The cardboard steps, the gripping hand, and the background stay fixed in place throughout, so all motion belongs to the moving chain. The cascade is still in progress on the upper steps, with the lowest spheres bouncing into the open air beside the staircase and still falling.
relations: Fingers holding the chain top -> chain pays out over the highest cardboard step.
Leading spheres tumbling over the edge -> cascading down vertical faces and rebounding off step edges.
Following spheres emerging from the hand -> stretching the chain longer as it feeds over each tier.
Fixed cardboard steps and background -> confining all motion to the descending, bouncing chain.
